name: Corrupted Kor Gem
summary: A Corrupted Kor Gem is a potent magical conduit warped by the dark rites of the naga residing around Blackfathom Deeps. Spellcasters covet such stones for their capacity to store sheer arcane force, though the gem's tainted state demands purification before it can serve righteous crafts.

sections.title: Vessels of Tainted Power
sections.body: Kor gems naturally possess the rare ability to capture and contain substantial magical energies, making them invaluable focuses for sorcerers and enchanted smithing. Along the coastline near the ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, however, the resident naga oracles and tide priestesses claim these gems for their own shadowy rituals. Through foul enchantments, the serpent-kin warp the stone, suffusing it with malevolent, sea-borne corruption. While this infusion taints the gem's nature, the core latent power remains potent, drawing those in need of exceptional magical foci to harvest them from the naga.

sections.title: Purification and Smithing
sections.body: A Corrupted Kor Gem cannot safely be worked into sacred implements without cleansing. Night elf sages, such as Thundris Windweaver of Auberdine, understand the ancient methods needed to scour away the naga's taint. Purifying the gem diminishes its volatile raw power to an extent, but stabilizes it so holy champions—most notably paladins forging blessed armaments under the guidance of artisans like Jordan Stilwell—can utilize the stone without succumbing to insidious darkness.

faq.q: What is a Kor Gem used for?
faq.answer: Kor gems act as powerful conduits and reservoirs for arcane energy. Spellcasters utilize them to hold immense reserves of power for their incantations, while skilled blacksmiths embed them into enchanted weapons to channel magical forces.

faq.q: Where are Corrupted Kor Gems found?
aliases: where to find corrupted kor gem
faq.answer: Corrupted Kor Gems are carried by naga spellcasters—specifically Blackfathom Tide Priestesses and Blackfathom Oracles—who dwell outside and within the ancient ruins leading to Blackfathom Deeps on the Ashenvale and Darkshore border.

faq.q: Why must the gem be purified?
faq.answer: The naga saturate the gems with foul magic during their rituals. Attempting to use a corrupted gem in sacred crafting could contaminate the forge or the wielder, requiring a master of nature or light, such as Thundris Windweaver, to purge the evil before it is worked into an arm.

faq.q: Does cleansing the gem weaken its power?
faq.answer: Yes. Removing the naga's taint purges the wild, malicious energy that bloated the gem, making the stone slightly weaker overall. However, the residual energy remains pure, stable, and strong enough for consecrated metalworking.

angles.text: Paladins seeking to forge sacred armaments must recover and purify a Kor Gem as a testament to their ability to confront evil and cleanse darkness into righteous strength.
Night elf scholars like Thundris Windweaver recognize the danger of naga relics encroaching on Darkshore and safeguard the knowledge needed to cleanse the ancient stones.
